s826.polar_choice: NTNU set chosen as default because it was measured in the turbine's own wind tunnel at a comparable turbulence level, on a large (c = 0.45 m, end dummies) model, and was published as BEM input for exactly these turbines. notes: ROTOR: 3 blades, NREL S826 (t/c 14 %) from r = 0.0675 m to the tip, blades milled in aluminium, pitch 0 in all tests, stall controlled, counter-clockwise rotation seen from upstream (irrelevant for BEM). The same blades were used on every NTNU blind-test turbine; the rotor diameter differs only by the hub: T2 (BT1, the downstream turbine of BT2-BT4, BT5) and LARS1 (BT5, Bartl 2018) D = 0.894 m; T1 (upstream turbine of BT2-BT4) D = 0.944 m (wider hub; not covered here). Krogstad & Lund 2012, Krogstad & Adaramola 2012 and Bartl 2018a state D = 0.90 m for the same rotor and normalise with it; their tsr, cp, ct were converted to R = 0.447 m (tsr x 0.447/0.45, cp and ct x (0.45/0.447)^2), the published values are kept in tsr_src/cp_src/ct_src columns, and rpm is the measured speed. The 3 mm ambiguity: the geometry table (Table C.1 of the BT5 invitation = Table I of Krogstad & Lund with R = 0.45 m) has 30 elements of 0.015 m whose outer edge is r = 0.450 m, while the stated BT1 diameter is 0.894 m (blade length 0.413 m + hub 0.068/2 m = 0.447 m). R = 0.447 m is used here with the table radii unchanged; the alternative (shift the table by -3 mm or use R = 0.45) changes CP by ~1 %. HUB/ROOT: nacelle/hub cover d = 90 mm (Rhub = 0.045 m; the BT5 invitation's 'Dhub = 0.068 m' is the blade-mounting hub inside the cover). Rows r = 0.0075/0.0225 m are inside the hub, the cylinder d = 13.5 mm is exposed from 0.045 to 0.049 m, a linear transition from 0.049 to 0.0675 m with a sharp corner, and the S826 from 0.0675 m. The tip is cut off square. TWIST is relative to the rotor plane (source convention = solver convention, no conversion); the source's twist 120 deg on the cylinder rows is a flag and is replaced by 38 deg. AIRFOIL DATA: the blades' Re is ~0.6e5-1.8e5 (tip Re ~1e5 at TSR 6, U 10 m/s; 3e4 at TSR 2). The S826 has strong low-Re effects below Re ~ 0.8e5 (laminar separation, static hysteresis); the DTU (low TI) and NTNU (TI 0.7 %) polars differ strongly in and after stall (DTU: abrupt stall at ~9 deg, cl_max 1.35; NTNU: cl_max ~1.5 at 13 deg, gentle), so the polar choice matters for TSR < 5. Sarmast & Mikkelsen's DTU report (2012/13, the polar the brief named) could not be downloaded (DTU Orbit/KTH DiVA block bots); Sarlak 2018 is the later, tabulated publication of the DTU measurements on the same wing (Sarlak 2014 shows the two DTU series agree). The METU data (Ostovan, Amiri & Uzol 2013, RUZGEM conference) were not found online. WIND TUNNEL: closed-return NTNU tunnel, test section 2.71 m wide x 1.80-1.85 m high (roof adjusted for zero pressure gradient), 11.15 m long; the BT1 paper says 'about 2 m high and almost 3 m wide'. Rotor-swept area 11.8-12.8 % of the section: NO blockage correction is applied to any of the data (the organisers deliberately leave the walls to the modellers; Sorensen & Mikkelsen's corrected BEM in BT1 changed CT by up to 10 %). Inflow TI 0.23-0.3 %, uniform within +-1 %. Air density: rho = 1.2 kg/m3 given by the organisers (BT5), viscosity not given (1.5e-5 m2/s assumed, air at ~20 C). CP is from a shaft torque transducer between rotor and bearings (bearing friction subtracted in the Bartl papers), CT = balance force minus the separately measured tower+nacelle drag. CP and CT independent of U for U > 9 m/s (Re-dependence file shows the drop at 7-9 m/s). LOADS: no blade or root-moment data were published for this rotor - Krogstad & Lund 2012 mention strain gauges for the root bending moment on one blade but write 'not included here'; only rotor thrust (and yaw moment My*, Bartl 2018b Fig. 1c / Muehle 2018 Table 3, not extracted since the BEM does not compute it) are available. The BT1 test also required spanwise load distributions at TSR 3, 6, 10, but only predictions (no measurements) were published. KARLSEN.BEM in the repo root is this rotor (B = 3, R = 0.45 m, design_tsr 7 (published design TSR 6), rho 1.225, nu 1.4207e-5): its 11 r/c/theta stations (r = 0.0075 ... 0.4425 m in 0.0435 m steps) are the published table resampled; 7 of the 9 S826 stations agree with linear interpolation of Table C.1 to < 0.001 deg / 0.01 mm, but r = 0.2685 m has twist 8.256 deg (table 8.525) and chord 0.04081 m (0.04076), and r = 0.3555 m has twist 4.366 deg (table 4.601) and chord 0.03130 m (0.03178) - probably spline-interpolated or typed from a figure. Further differences: Rhub = 0.006 m (physical hub/nacelle cover radius 0.045 m); the cylinder chord is 0.030 m (table: 0.0135 m - Krogstad & Lund give c/R = 0.03, i.e. the .bem took c/R as metres) and r = 0.051 m (in the transition, table chord 0.0255 m) is labelled 'Circle'; the 'Circle' twist values 120 / 92.67 deg are the source's flag value 120 interpolated, not a geometric angle; R = 0.45 m (the K&L value) instead of 0.447 m.
